title: Abdominal pain in a woman of childbearing age
setting: Community health clinic triage room, mid-morning
description: A 27-year-old woman presents with worsening left-sided lower abdominal pain and dizziness.

speaker.name: Naledi Mokoena
speaker.style: Polite and anxious. She answers questions but is initially private about her sexual and menstrual history. She downplays her dizziness until asked directly.

patient.name: Naledi Mokoena
patient.living_situation: Lives with her partner in a nearby township

presenting_complaint: Sharp pain in the left lower abdomen since this morning, getting worse, with light-headedness.
opening_line: Sister, this pain in my tummy is getting worse. It is here on the left, low down, and I feel a bit light-headed.
personality: Anxious, polite, and guarded about sensitive history. She becomes more forthcoming when treated respectfully and given privacy.

history.onset: Sudden onset about six hours ago while she was at work; the pain has steadily worsened.
history.character: Sharp, stabbing left lower abdominal pain, severity 8 out of 10. Nothing relieves it; paracetamol did not help.
history.radiation: The pain sometimes spreads to her left shoulder tip.
associated_symptoms: missed period for about seven weeks
history.menstrual_history: Usually regular. Last period was about seven weeks ago. She has not done a pregnancy test.
history.sexual_history: Sexually active with one partner. No contraception, or inconsistent condom use. She is not sure whether she could be pregnant.
history.past_medical_history: No chronic illness, no previous surgery, no previous pregnancies.
history.medications: Paracetamol taken earlier today. No regular medication.
history.social_history: Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol. Works as a cashier and lives with her partner.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Suspected ectopic pregnancy, possibly leaking or ruptured
red_flags: sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain
expected_actions: urgent referral or ambulance to an emergency department with obstetric cover
check observations including pulse, blood pressure, and level of consciousness
keep the patient nil by mouth and monitor while awaiting transfer
clear safety-netting and do not send home

learning_objectives: Take a focused abdominal and pregnancy history
Recognise the red flags of an obstetric emergency
Prioritise urgent escalation over routine assessment
Discuss sensitive history with privacy and empathy
